paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: move big tool results to disk, keep their head inline, let the model pull t
he rest back with recall(id).
# dsh-recall
## Why
Measured on 8 504 tool results from real sessions:
| fact | value |

| results larger than 6 KB | 4.6% of results |
| …and their share of all tool-result characters | 40

.7% |
| …that are never opened again | 76% |

So the expensive part of a coding session is a handful of huge results that nobody reads twice.
Offl

oading them removes tokens that would otherwise be **re-sent on every later step**: the saving
is `r
emoved_tokens × remaining_steps × cache_price`, not `removed_tokens`.

Ceiling, stated plainly: tool results are roughly 46% of the context, so offloading *all* of them
st

ill caps at about 18% of the context. On a route that bills cache reads near input price that is
a r

eal 20–25% of a long session; on a first-party route with a cheap cache it is single digits, and
the
re the lever is fresh input and step count instead.
## Features

- **Head and tail, not just head** — the tail is where tools put their own retrieval notices and
sum

maries. A head-only cut throws that away, so the stock spill notice
(`Full formatted result stored a

t: …`) is kept whole, opening paren included.
- **Budget gate** — optionally offload only while the

surface actually exceeds a token budget
(`budgetTokens`), so nothing is shortened for a saving that

was not needed.
- **Replay-safe rewrite** — the same pair the stock pruner uses: a `compaction/prune

` event that
prices and cites the shadowed node, then a `tool/result` with `surfaceOp: {op:'replace'

mpotence** — the store remembers which `(session, seq)` pairs were offloaded, so a
tool that merely

*prints* the `[recall]` marker cannot make the reaper skip a genuine result.
- **Non-text blocks sur

vive** — images in a tool result ride along untouched; only text is shortened.
- **Code-point safe**

— slices and counts use Unicode code points, so a surrogate pair is never split
down the middle.
-

**Searchable recall** — `recall(id, query: "…")` returns matching lines with their real character
of

fsets, so the model can jump straight to the spot instead of bisecting a 200 KB log.
- **Deduplicate

d, compressed store** — one SQLite file, payloads deflated and keyed by the SHA-256 of
the raw text:

the same output read twice is stored once.
- **Retention that exists** — `maxAgeDays` and `maxBytes

` evict oldest-first and reclaim the blobs
nobody references any more.
- **Exact token accounting**

— savings are priced by the harness token meter, not by `chars / 4`.
- **The strip** — a compact pil

l in `shell.overlay` with offloads, tokens kept out of context, recall
hits and the on-disk footprin

t.
- **Degrades instead of breaking** — an unreadable or unsupported store logs one line, the profil

e
loads, and `recall` says the store is unavailable.
## Requirements

| `dsh` | `>= 0.2.0-0` (declared in `package.json`) |
| Node | `>= 22.5` for the object store (`node

:sqlite` is a standard-library module) |
| Profile | any for the host half; a **web** profile for th
e strip (`dsh.client.platform: web`) |
On older Node the plugin still loads and the `recall` tool still answers — it just reports that the
store is unavailable, because there is no SQLite to put it in.
### What happens to a big result

1. A tool result lands on the surface.
2. On the next tool call, every result **older than the newes

t `keep`** and **longer than
`thresholdChars`** is rewritten to `head + [recall] note + tail`.
3. Th
e middle is written to the store under `md5(session:seq:chars)[:8]`, e.g. `#4d3661d2`.
The model sees this instead of 4 000 characters of output:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Nothing is deleted: the full text stays in the session log and in the store.
## How it works
The reaper is a `tools/post-execute` waterfall listener — the same hook the stock spill policy uses:

1. take the surface snapshot and find the `tool/result` nodes;
2. drop the newest `keep` and anythin

g at or below `thresholdChars`;
3. for each candidate, derive the message, cut it to head and tail,

rices and cites the shadowed node) and then `tool/result` with
`surfaceOp: {op:'replace', startSeq,

endSeq}` and `sourceEventSeqs: [seq]`;
5. record the object in the store and stop when the token bud

rceEventSeqs: [seq]`;
5. record the object in the store and stop when the token budget is satisfied.

Two details keep the hot path cheap: a per-session set of already-judged seqs (so a result is
derive

d once, not on every tool call), and prepared statements in the store (the candidate check is
an ind
exed lookup, not a parse).
## What this is not: the 15% compaction
`dsh-recall` never decides *when* the context gets compressed and never touches the context window.
The percentage-based compression is the stock `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic` plugin, configured
in the profile's own patch layer (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations
- **A pointer is only useful while the head still explains the result.** That is why the note carrie

s
the tool name and the full size.
- **The last big result of a session is never offloaded.** The ho

ok runs before the current result
enters the surface, so the reaper only sees older ones; something

newer has to arrive first.
- **Text blocks collapse into one.** Multi-text-block results keep their

text in order and their
images, but an image that sat *between* two text blocks moves after them.
-

**The `[recall]` marker is a conservative pre-filter.** A genuine result that happens to contain
the

literal `[recall]` is left alone.
- **Resumed sessions start with an empty `callId → name` map**, s

o a result offloaded right after a
restart may be labelled `tool` instead of `read`. Cosmetic.
- **R

etention breaks old pointers by construction.** With `maxBytes`/`maxAgeDays` set, a deleted
object a

nswers `not found`.
- **Two harness instances share one pool.** SQLite serializes their writes (`bus

y_timeout`); every
displayed number except `recalls` is derived, so they cannot disagree.
